messages:
maria: Thinking out loud — propose we add a per-tier circuit-breaker for routing that trips on a combination of token-quota consumption rate + model error-rate. Purpose: avoid cascading costs for free tier and protect pro customers from noisy tenants.

ajay: +1. do you mean a hard cut or staged degradation?

maria: staged — first try cheaper variant (quantized / distilled) -> if still failing or errors spike, move to reject with clear 429 body. soft degrade for pro, hard for free by default.

kevin: can we avoid surprises for customers? need telemetry and dashboard visible state (open/closed/half-open). Uptime SLA customers should get opt-out or higher thresholds.

sarah: agree, we also need an admin override API for on-call to flip breaker per-tenant. It has to be auditable (who/why).

maria: sketch of policy object (console + API can edit):
```json
{
  "tier": "free|pro|enterprise",
  "thresholds": {
    "tokens_per_minute": 2000,
    "error_rate_pct": 5
  },
  "degradation_steps": [
    "variant:quantized-8bit",
    "variant:small-dedicated",
    "reject:reason:circuit_breaker"
  ],
  "canary_percent": 5,
  "audit_log_enabled": true
}
```

ajay: love the steps. two questions: 1) how do we measure error_rate (model logits NaN? upstream timeouts? high perplexity?) 2) how does `canary_percent` interact with routing weights?

kevin: error_rate should be composite: grpc/timeout errors, abnormal token generation (e.g., >X tokens/sec), and eval-qa regression alerts. We'll need a tag in telemetry to attribute which metric tripped. Canary_percent should mean we only apply steps to X% of traffic until stable. routing weight adjustments should be done in runtime router, not manual edits.

sarah: UX: console should show a timeline, current step, sample requests that matched the rule, and a one-click rollback (flip to previous step). Also surfacing cost delta estimate when moving to cheaper variant.

maria: operational concerns: 1) policy evaluation must be cheap (runtime) — keep rule set small and compile to matcher bytecode. 2) fallback variants must be compatible (vocab, tokenizer, sequence length). 3) telemetry retention for these events should be 90d by default for enterprise, 14d for free.

deploy-bot: [deploy] routing-engine-v2 rollout to canary fraction 2% in us-west at 2026-03-18T09:12:23Z

ajay: propose API knobs: POST /admin/tenants/{id}/circuit-breaker (body: action: open/close/step/override, reason, expires_at). return current policy and active step. All calls go to audit log.

maria: agreed. For canary rollout plan: start with internal-only tenants -> opt-in beta customers -> 5% random -> 25% -> 100%. Need a rollback window and automatic rewind if error_rate worsens by >2x for 10m.

kevin: telemetry story: generate events with fields [tenant_id, tier, rule_id, step_applied, metric_values, sample_request_id]. We'll add a dedicated dashboard: CB heatmap by region+tier and a table for recent trips. Alerting: when enterprise tenants see a trip, page SRE + account owner.

sarah: console UI: make default rules per-tier but editable at tenant level. Add copy-from-tier quick action and validation that ensures compatibility (e.g., variant supports seq_len).

ajay: runtime implementation notes: evaluate policies in router pre-routing stage so we can short-circuit variant selection. Keep state in Redis with TTL windows for half-open semantics. Use token-bucket counters per-tenant for rate.

maria: dev plan: week1 spec + telemetry schema, week2 console mocks + API proto, week3 runtime impl + canary, week4 rollout and docs. Who wants to own spec?

kevin: I can own telemetry and dashboard.

ajay: I'll own runtime changes and API proto.

sarah: I'll do console design and UX validation with PM.

maria: thanks — I'll draft the spec doc today and ping respective owners. tagging @kevin @ajay @sarah for sync. :thumbsup:
